accountId.description: An account's id on its environment: a version 4 UUID the environment mints when it adopts or adds the account; an account carried over from configuration keeps the id it was configured with.

total.description: The sessions the account's directory holds, as its adapter lists them.

archived.description: Of them, those that import archived: tagged archived, or begun by the provider's scheduler.

missingDirectory.description: Of them, those whose working directory is gone.

new.description: Of them, those this environment does not hold yet, by provider session id: what an import brings in.

sessions.description: The sessions Carry over finds in an adopted account's directory: every one, the archived, those with a missing directory, and the new.

folders.description: The memory folders the directory holds with at least one file in them.

repositories.description: The repositories they map to: the distinct auto-memory keys (the repository identity, else the main checkout, else the workspace path) of the folders a transcript, or an assignment, maps.

folder.description: The project folder the memory lies in, by its name under projects/: what carryOver.assignMemory takes.

path.description: The memory folder itself, projects/<folder>/memory in the adopted directory.

items.description: A memory folder of the adopted directory: its project folder's name and its path.

unmappable.description: The folders with no transcript left in their project folder to name the path, and no assignment: carryOver.assignMemory copies one. Its length is the count.

new.description: Of the mapped folders, those an import would copy: new, or changed since an import last copied them.

memory.description: The memory Carry over finds in an adopted account's directory: its folders, the repositories they map to, the unmappable, and the new.

skills.description: The skill folders found, the offered checkouts among them, invalid ones left out: in the adopted directory's skills/ and the machine's ~/.agents/skills.

commands.description: The command files found in the adopted directory's commands/, invalid ones left out.

new.description: Of them, those a run would copy into the own directory: the rest it keeps out, the own directory holding their name, or offers as sources.

name.description: A skill's name, by the Agent Skills rule: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and -, with no leading, trailing or doubled hyphen. Refused as invalid_params, the issue's params naming the rule skill-name and its reason.

from.description: Where the skill folder was found: in the adopted directory's skills/, or in the machine's ~/.agents/skills.

url.description: The working tree's remote, as git expands it, stripped of any credential.

folder.description: The skill folder's path in the repository, from its root; . when the folder is the repository's root.

anyOf.description: A branch a skill source follows, as git takes a branch name: 1 to 255 characters with no white space, control character or any of ~ ^ : ? * [ \, no .. or @{, no empty segment, none beginning with . or ending with .lock, no trailing / or ., not @, and not beginning with -.

branch.description: The branch; null for the remote's default branch, the one its HEAD names.

oneOf.description: A branch the source syncs from, at start, every six hours and on Pull now.

commit.description: A git commit's full object name: 40 lowercase hexadecimal digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository.

oneOf.description: A commit the source is pinned to: it never syncs until it is unpinned.

follow.description: The branch the working tree is on (its upstream's on the remote, else the local one), or a pin at its commit when HEAD is detached.

items.description: A skill folder inside a git working tree with a remote, offered as a skill source instead of copied: the URL, folder and follow skills.sources.add takes.

offered.description: The skill folders inside a git working tree with a remote, offered as sources rather than copied.

invalid.description: The skill folders and command files that read as invalid, which a run leaves where they are.

skills.description: The skills and commands Carry over finds, as skills.carryOver's dry run answers them: counted, the new, the checkouts offered as sources, and the invalid.

kind.description: What it is: subagent, a Markdown file in the adopted directory's agents/; plugin, an installed plugin its plugins/ lists.

name.description: Its name: a subagent's file name without .md; a plugin's as its installed list names it, name@marketplace.

items.description: A subagent or plugin in the adopted directory, which Carry over does not carry.

notCarried.description: The directory's subagents and plugins, listed by name as not carried.

hooks.description: The hook commands the directory's settings.json declares, across its events and matchers.

mcpServers.description: The personal MCP servers the provider's global config declares: at user scope, and at local scope for each project.

permissionRules.description: The permission rules the directory's settings.json lists: allow, ask and deny together.

doesNotCarry.description: What does not carry, counted in the adopted directory: its hooks, its personal MCP servers and its permission rules. The terminal client keeps using them.

anyOf.description: What Carry over's card counts in an adopted account's directory: its sessions, memory, skills and commands, the subagents and plugins not carried, and the hooks, personal MCP servers and permission rules that do not carry.

sharedProjectsWith.description: Source id owning the shared projects folder; its sessions and memory are offered once.
